def iso_date(year, month, day):

The date formatting helper produces ambiguous output because it uses the format 'month/day/year', which can be ambiguous in some cases (e.g., February 28 vs. March 2).

To fix this issue, you can use the ISO 8601 format, which is 'year-month-day'. However, since you want to keep the original format, you can add a check to ensure that the day is not greater than the last day of the month.

```python
import calendar

def iso_date(year, month, day):
    if day > calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]:
        raise ValueError("Invalid day for the given month and year")
    return f'{month}/{day}/{year}'
```

This code will raise a ValueError if the day is not valid for the given month and year, preventing the production of ambiguous output.
